name: [Carto] AI guardrail denying agent actions
message:
{{#is_alert}}
**The AI guardrail is refusing agent actions on pillar `{{[@pillar].name}}`.**

{{value}} denials in the last 15 minutes.

A denial is the guardrail WORKING, so this is informational unless the rate is new. What it usually means per pillar:

- `identity` — an agent is calling without a valid attestation, or acting on an order with nobody signed in. Check whether an agent was deployed without its token.
- `authority` — an agent is attempting something outside its granted scope. If this is sudden, someone changed what the agent tries to do without changing its grants.
- `condition` — preconditions failing. A spike usually means upstream order state is not what the agent believes it is.
- `budget` — a session hit its spend ceiling. Investigate a runaway loop before raising the ceiling.
- `evidence` — actions that cannot be audited. This one is never benign: it means decisions are being made that nobody can reconstruct afterwards.

Decision trail: the evaluator writes every pillar verdict to `guardrail_decisions`, joinable to the order by `@order_id` and across the fulfilment seam by `@txn_id`.

- Logs: `service:carto-guardrails @guardrail_decision:deny`
- Traces: `service:carto-guardrails` then the `guardrail.*` spans
- In the app: /guardrails
{{/is_alert}}
{{#is_recovery}}
Denials on `{{[@pillar].name}}` are back under the threshold.
{{/is_recovery}}
